oracle.layout: src/tmlm/ssl/hao_diag.py docstring: positive (even) clauses hold OR-group c in node c, one word per alternative, alternatives beyond the group size repeat the group's words; negative (odd) clauses: with negated literals 'group g missing' (all 6 negated words of g in every leaf, g = clause pair index mod 4); with positive literals only, clause 1 is a constant-1 bias clause and the other odd clauses never fire; weights 1 - 2 x (clause mod 2), the package's own vanilla initialisation
oracle.depth_note: deep: included TAs at 2^bits - 1, excluded at 0 (the PRIMARY depth: maximal margin); boundary: included at 2^(bits-1), excluded at 2^(bits-1) - 1 (the package's own initial value)
oracle.other_hyperparameters: as in the installed commit's tuned config for that model (T, clauses, alternatives, state bits, boost, switches); only s is replaced
oracle.write: fresh machine; the package's allocate_gpu_memory and initialize_weights_and_ta_states (exactly what the first fit() does); then pycuda memcpy_htod into ta_state_hierarchy_gpu and clause_weights_gpu; first = False. The package's own load(state_dict) (both commits: allocate_gpu_memory, the same two memcpy_htod, first = False) would give the same state: it only skips initialize_weights_and_ta_states, whose prepare_weights draws no random number for a non-coalesced TsetlinMachine (weights 1 - 2 x (clause mod 2)) and whose prepare_hierarchy output the copy overwrites [verified in source: tm.py load and kernels.py prepare_weights at c85ca4e7 and 5b4a223]; the direct copies are kept because they reproduce the first fit() step by step and are verified by read-back. Not set_state: at both commits it allocates number_of_clauses x number_of_ta_teams x number_of_state_bits x 4 bytes, a factor number_of_literal_chunks_per_leaf (125 with negated literals, 63 without, at 2,000 features) too small, so its memcpy_htod of a full-size state writes past the end of that allocation (an out-of-bounds device write: undefined behaviour, a CUDA error or silent corruption of neighbouring device buffers); and it leaves first = True, so the next fit() re-allocates and re-initialises (audited from source by hao_diag.set_state_allocation, in tests on both sources and at run time on the installed one)

stable_rule.text: a cell is STABLE iff all 50 epochs ran and at epoch 50 the unseen-combination accuracy is >= 0.95 AND the mean per-node Jaccard of the positive clauses against the oracle's node identities is >= 0.90

reading_notes.written: 2026-09-25, before any output of experiments/ssl_r2_hao_diagnostics.py; amended the same day, still before any output (see written_before_any_output)

demos.text: a demo variant PASSES iff all its planned runs completed the default epochs and their mean final test accuracy is >= 0.95. The primary rows are the hierarchical variants; the vanilla rows are the author's own flat comparison and are reported, not judged. A failed hierarchical demo at a commit means the package fails its author's own positive control there (with this seeded port), and no H-AO failure at that commit is attributed to the H-AO world

seen_unseen.text: at the final (tuned) epoch: MEMORISES COMBINATIONS iff seen minus unseen accuracy >= 0.10; MEMORISES BAGS iff fit minus seen accuracy >= 0.10; GENERALISES TO UNSEEN COMBINATIONS iff unseen accuracy >= 0.90 and |seen minus unseen| < 0.05. A model with a large combination gap learned combinations, not OR-groups; H17.5's held-out test combinations are all unseen, so its registered accuracy tracks the unseen column
seen_unseen.seed100_bias: at world seed 100 the unseen bags are EXACTLY the validation bags (stream 4) on which every tuned configuration (hyperparameters and chosen epoch) was selected, so seed-100 unseen accuracies are biased upward by that choice and the seed-100 flags are optimistic; world seed 101 (a new world, new combinations, new bags) is the unbiased reading. The report marks every seed-100 row unseen_is_tuning_validation = true
seen_unseen.unseen_fresh: unseen_fresh (stream 22) are 4,000 new bags of the same validation combinations, never used by any tuning run; they are reported next to unseen at both seeds, with the same two flags computed on them (memorises_combinations_fresh, generalises_to_unseen_combinations_fresh). At seed 100 they remove the bag-level selection bias but not the combination-level one (the configurations were still chosen on these combinations)
seen_unseen.controls: the controls stage (tmu_tm, tmu_ctm, lr, gbt, mlp, params.controls) gets the same columns and flags; the rows are controls and carry no verdict of their own: the question of A8 3 (ii) is about the package, the controls say whether a non-hierarchical learner separates seen from unseen combinations on the same bags

pospair.text: per commit and world seed at the final epoch: HIERARCHY HELPS WHERE FLAT CANNOT EXPRESS COMPACTLY iff hier minus flat unseen accuracy >= 0.10 and hier unseen accuracy >= 0.75; NEITHER LEARNS iff both fit accuracies are < 0.60; otherwise NO HIERARCHY ADVANTAGE. Derived expectation stated now: a flat positive-literal machine that only stores 4-word conjunctions of seen combinations fires on no unseen positive, so its unseen positive accuracy is 0 and its unseen accuracy is at most about 0.5 plus its negative accuracy share

oracle.factorial_trigger: the A8 width, distractor and sample-size factorial is added iff some (commit, model, s) cell of the DEEP oracle is STABLE (params.oracle.stable_rule) on BOTH world seeds 100 and 101
oracle.text: per (commit, model, depth, s): a cell whose write was not verified (read-back, package equal to the numpy reference, prediction >= 0.95) is INVALID and says nothing about stability. If no deep cell is stable at any s, the true hierarchy is not a fixed point of the package's learning rule on H-AO at the tuned hyperparameters: learning it from scratch is then not expected at those settings, whatever the tuning. If deep cells are stable but boundary cells are not, the truth is stable only with a large margin (a narrow basin). The per-node Jaccard curve tells whether decay starts in the OR nodes (words dropped or distractors added) or in the negative clauses (de_morgan Jaccard)
oracle.node_jaccard_note: the positive-clause node Jaccard (pos_node_jaccard_mean, part of the stable rule) counts POSITIVE literals only: the words of node c with an included positive literal against group c. Negated literals that the package adds to positive clauses (it can, with append_negated, at T = 1e5) do not change it; they show up in literals_added (per role) and in clauses_exact_share. So STABLE means stable in function (unseen accuracy >= 0.95) and in positive-literal node identity, not bit-identical to the oracle; clauses_exact_share and literals_added say how far from bit-identical a stable cell is

threshold.text: REACHED at the first evaluated epoch with fit accuracy >= 0.95 (resolution 10 epochs), else NOT REACHED within 2 GPU-hours with the last fit, seen and unseen accuracies reported; the package's own noisy-parity demo needs about 7,780 epochs for 99.71 percent (docs/13 A8 3 (iv)), so NOT REACHED within 2 hours is not read as 'never'

valiant.text: Valiant elimination LEARNS THE CONCEPT on a world seed iff, with all positive fit bags, its unseen-combination accuracy is >= 0.95 and all 4 true OR-groups are among its minimal surviving ORs. If it does, the AND-of-OR concept is learnable from these positive bags by a logic-native learner with no Tsetlin automata, and a package failure on the same bags is a failure of the package's learning dynamics, not of the data. Its negatives are always right while the 4 true groups survive (a negative misses a whole group); its errors are unseen positives rejected by spurious ORs that the seen combinations did not eliminate
